benchmark_evidence.notes: new-benchmark: devstral-2-human-winrate not yet in data/benchmarks/. Vendor-commissioned human preference evaluation (42.8% win and 28.6% loss are both Devstral 2's own rates against DeepSeek V3.2, not DeepSeek scores, so no separate comparison_cited row). Same section states Claude Sonnet 4.5 'remains significantly preferred' with no numbers printed. Task set, sample size, and eval duration are not stated on the page.

notes: Page fetched via web-reader; page metadata carries no timestamp - release date taken from the official mistral.ai RSS feed (pubDate Tue, 09 Dec 2025 12:00:00 GMT). 'Up to 7x more cost-efficient than Claude Sonnet at real-world tasks' (Highlights) and size comparisons vs DeepSeek V3.2 / Kimi K2 are parameter-count and cost claims, not benchmark scores, so no rows. Page recommends temperature 0.2 for optimal performance, but ties it to Mistral Vibe CLI deployment best practices rather than stating it as the benchmark protocol, so protocol.temperature stays null. The SWE-bench chart images (open weights vs proprietary; performance vs model size) are not machine-read. 2026-09-01 audit: all three row values re-verified verbatim against the live page (72.2% / 68.0% SWE-bench Verified in Highlights + body; 42.8% win / 28.6% loss vs DeepSeek V3.2 in the human-eval section); release date 2025-12-09 re-confirmed from the official RSS pubDate (Tue, 09 Dec 2025 12:00:00 GMT); page title matches. Remaining page numbers are parameter-count comparisons (5x/28x vs DeepSeek V3.2, 8x/41x vs Kimi K2) and the 7x cost-efficiency claim - correctly not benchmark rows. SWE-bench competitor values live only in the two chart images (open-weights vs proprietary; performance vs model size) with no printed labels, so no comparison rows.
